title: SLO-driven dynamic hysteresis and safe fallback policy engine
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: Implement a policy engine that derives per-entity (dependency/model/tenant) circuit breaker thresholds from SLOs and runtime signals, applies hysteresis windows to avoid flapping, and coordinates safe fallback behavior (model variant reroutes, cached prefixes, regional failover) with an observable rollout. This ticket scopes the policy, runtime hooks, rollout strategy, and verification harness; separate tickets will implement storage and UI surfaces.
motivation: Current hard-coded trip thresholds are brittle: tenants and models have different latency/error budgets and capacity characteristics. We want thresholds that adapt to the SLOs we promise and to observed capacity, reduce false-positive tripping during transient spikes, and ensure any fallback path is safe (doesn't violate data locality or exceed dedicated capacity).
proposal: 1) Define mapping rules: for each entity derive thresholds from active SLOs (error budget burn-rate, p50/p95 latency targets, GPU queue depth). 2) Use adaptive hysteresis windows (short for severe violations, longer for marginal ones) to prevent oscillation. 3) On trip, execute a deterministic fallback plan ordered by safety: local cache hit -> cheaper model-variant (quantized/shorter context) pinned for a cohort -> regional reroute -> graceful reject with structured error and suggested retry-after. 4) Expose policy as a JSON spec stored in config service; runtime reads cached copy and honors safe-fallback constraints (data residency, tenant tier).
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine computes thresholds from SLO metadata for at least three test tenants and two model families
Hysteresis prevents flip-flop under intermittent load spikes in the canary cluster (2hr soak)
Fallback actions executed in correct safety order and are logged with reason codes
Observed p95 latency and error-rate for protected routes remain within SLO during controlled degradation tests
Monitoring dashboard shows the derived thresholds, current windowed metrics, and recent fallback events
design_notes:
- Threshold synthesis uses: (error_budget_fraction * historical_baseline_error_rate) and latency headroom scaled by inverse capacity_utilization.
- Hysteresis = max(30s, adaptive_factor * detection_window) where adaptive_factor depends on severity.
- Fallback actions include surface-level constraints: cannot reroute to region if tenant has 'region_locked' flag; cannot choose quantized variant for requests with 'high_precision' label.
- All fallback actions must emit structured event with fields: entity_key, reason_code, previous_thresholds, action_taken, target_node/model_variant, correlation_id.
implementation_plan: Spec: create policy schema and unit conversion rules (1 sprint)
Runtime hooks: implement evaluation pipeline in serving-runtime that consults policy and metrics (2 sprints)
Fallback adapters: implement model-variant selector, prefix-cache fastpath, and regional reroute client (2 sprints)
Observability: add metrics, traces, and dashboard panels (1 sprint)
Canary & Validation: staged rollout with load simulation and chaos experiments (1 sprint)
work_items: ENG-63249: schema: policy spec and validation
ENG-63252: fallback adapters (cache / variant selector / rerouter)
ENG-63254: canary pipeline + load test harness
notes: Keep config size bounded — policies should compile to O(1) rules per tenant+model in the hot path. Avoid expensive DB hops during evaluation (use local LRU cache with TTL).
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for threshold derivation math with edge cases (zero baseline, very small error budget). 2) Integration tests injecting synthetic metrics (latency/error/utilization) to assert computed thresholds and hysteresis windows. 3) Controlled chaos: kill workers and validate safe fallback sequence and SLA preservation. 4) Performance test to ensure policy evaluation adds <1ms median to request path for common case.
monitoring_and_alerting: Emit metrics: derived_threshold_{err,latency,util}_per_key, hysteresis_state{open,closing,closed}, fallback_actions_count_by_type, fallback_latencies. Alerts: when fallback rate > 0.5% of qps for >5m for paid tenants; when policy evaluation latency >5ms p99.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 0: Dry-run mode where derived thresholds are computed and logged but not enforced (1 week).
- Phase 1: Canary on non-critical orgs (5% traffic) with automatic rollback on safety signals (error-rate spike or SLO regressions) (2 weeks).
- Phase 2: Progressive ramp by tenant cohorts with health gates (30% -> 60% -> 100%).
- Phase 3: Enable multi-region reroute fallback after 50% of tenants successfully use local fallbacks.
observability_playbook: If a fallback action triggers, oncall runbook: 1) Query event stream for correlation_id to see preceding metric windows. 2) Check config: was policy changed in last 30m? 3) If fallback is region-reroute, check capacity in target region. 4) If unexpected repeated fallbacks, consider manually increasing hysteresis for affected entity and open incident to investigate model regression.
security_and_compliance: Policy engine must respect tenant region_lock and data_class flags. No fallback may send PII-bearing requests to a region not authorized by tenant. All fallback decision logs are forwarded to audit logs with tenant id and must be retained according to compliance retention policy.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly aggressive fallbacks cause degraded UX — Mitigation: start in dry-run, use conservative default thresholds and require two independent signals before enforcing.
Risk: Flapping due to correlated upstream noise — Mitigation: hysteresis windows tuned by severity and cross-entity dampening to avoid cascading trips.
Risk: Misrouted data during regional reroute — Mitigation: honor region_lock flags and add pre-checks against tenant allowed-regions list.
Risk: Increased tail latencies from policy evaluation — Mitigation: cache compiled policy and evaluate with optimized hot-path code; performance budget: p99 < 5ms.

Risk: Too many model-variant fallbacks consuming dedicated capacity — Mitigation: quota fallback limits per-tenant and backpressure signals to refuse additional fallbacks when capacity thresholds reached.
